data.name: Home.Body
data.value:
BoxedWine opens Windows programs (.exe, .bat, .cmd, .msi) and DOS programs (.com). They run in a virtual machine of Os-x86, never in Kazo OS itself.
Double-click a program in the File Explorer, or choose “Open a program…”.

data.name: Tutorial.Step1.Body
data.value:
BoxedWine opens Windows programs (.exe, .bat, .cmd, .msi) and DOS programs (.com) in Kazo OS.
The programs do not run in Kazo itself: Os-x86 runs them in a virtual machine, with its own permissions. BoxedWine is the window that shows them.

data.name: Tutorial.Step1.Title
data.value: Welcome to BoxedWine

data.name: Tutorial.Step2.Body
data.value:
Double-click an .exe file in the File Explorer, choose “Open with ▸ BoxedWine”, or open it from the Terminal with “xdg-open ./setup.exe”. The “Open a program…” button does the same.
For now BoxedWine launches console programs: their output shows in the window, and you write to them in the bottom line. Ctrl+C interrupts the program; closing the window ends it. The first time, Os-x86 downloads its Windows image: starting then takes a minute.

data.name: Tutorial.Step2.Title
data.value: Launch a program

data.name: Tutorial.Step3.Body
data.value:
BoxedWine does not look for the programs you install by itself: you add them yourself.
The “Add an application to Kazo OS” menu will let you choose the executable or the shortcut (.lnk) of an installed program. It will get an entry in the Start menu and, if you want, a shortcut on the desktop. This menu comes in a later version; until then, keep your programs in your files and open them with a double-click.
You can see this tutorial again with the “Tutorial” button.
